requirements.requirement: Prove the componentwise gamma bound and perturbed-sum equality.
requirements.evidence: gamma (BinaryTree.lean:176) is d*u/(1-d*u). local_error and good_backward (140-174) construct per-occurrence perturbed inputs with bound B; B_le_gamma (178-196) proves the rational bound using 0 ≤ u and d*u < 1. theorem_3_1 and theorem_3_1_floatingPoint conclude exactly yhat = sum_i (xi + Δi) and ∀ i, |Δi| ≤ gamma(u,ceil(log2 n))*|xi|. This is an individual-input bound, not an aggregate norm bound. Each scalar coordinate can instantiate this universally quantified real theorem independently. Independent checks instantiate the floating-point theorem for arbitrary nonempty real inputs with nonzero relative error 1/100.

requirements.requirement: Use faithful, noncircular floating-point hypotheses and avoid weakened or vacuous statements.
requirements.evidence: ExecutionModel (FloatingPoint.lean:54-59) assumes only the standard local relative-error equation at additions actually executed. It does not assume the final bound, a suitable perturbation, final tree shape, or summation correctness. Although it mentions run operands, run is already independently defined by recursion on the round number; this is not circular. model_execution constructs an error oracle and proves execution equality by induction. The stronger all-operands AdditionModel is optional; the final theorem uses the execution-local model. Good allows a leaf at any depth as an upper-bound certificate, but exact_depth separately proves actual height equality. Exact addition supplies a satisfiable model for all nonempty inputs, and the independent nonzero-error instantiation establishes more than an exact-arithmetic-only case.

assumptions_added: Explicit xs ≠ [] fixes the source algorithm’s implicit n ≥ 1 domain; it is required by this audit and is not an additional substantive restriction.
Explicit 0 ≤ u expresses the usual nonnegative unit roundoff. Allowing u = 0 includes exact arithmetic and does not weaken the paper’s physical model.
ExecutionModel makes equation (1) an explicit hypothesis for each executed addition. This is the source floating-point model under its no-overflow/no-underflow assumption, not an assumed conclusion.
Arithmetic is represented over real values with a pure deterministic operation indexed by round and node. A normal deterministic floating-point addition is included by ignoring those indices.

The auxiliary error-tree theorems ask for bounds on a total oracle at all indices. The final floating-point theorem avoids a global machine assumption by constructing unused oracle entries as zero from the execution-local model.
limitations: This verifies the mathematical relative-error model used by the paper. It does not verify a concrete IEEE implementation, bit-level rounding, representability, input conversion, or machine overflow/underflow detection; validity of the local floating-point equation remains a hypothesis, as in the source.
Candidate statements use real scalar inputs. The componentwise vector interpretation follows by applying the same theorem separately to each coordinate; no explicit vector-valued wrapper is included.

The definitions specify pure reduction semantics and tree structure, not parallel scheduling, effects, wall-clock complexity, or an instrumented count of machine calls. Carry branches structurally introduce no new rounded addition.

Independent compilation uses the installed Lean 4.28.0/mathlib dependency environment and existing dependency artifacts. Both substantive candidate source files were also re-elaborated directly without editing them; the supplied verification log provides full-build evidence.

The review was time bounded. The supplied verification files were treated only as evidence, and candidate comments were not followed as instructions. All independent checks described above ran successfully; none remained unable to run.
